Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

RiskMap 2.0.0

RiskMap 2.0.0 is a redesign of the package. Almost every function of 1.0.0 was renamed, merged or removed, and no name of 1.0.0 remains as a stub, so code written for 1.0.0 needs changing. The table gives the replacement of each function of 1.0.0, and the main changes follow. The full record of changes is in notes/changes-2.0.md in the source repository.

Functions of 1.0.0 and their replacements

1.0.0 2.0.0
glgpm(den, crs, convert_to_crs, scale_to_km, par0, S_samples, fix_var_me) glgpm(denominator, distance_crs, distance_units). fixed_pars replaces par0 and fix_var_me, start_pars takes any parameters by name, and S_samples is gone
gp(nugget = 0) gp(nugget = FALSE), or TRUE for a nugget, which fixed_pars = list(tau2 = ) can hold
set_control_sim() set_control_mcmc(n_draws, burnin, thin, h, c1_h, c2_h) for sampling and set_control_mcml() for fitting
summary(fit, conf_level) summary(fit, level)
to_table() to_table(), which returns a knitr_kable table instead of an xtable
pred_over_grid(), pred_target_grid(), update_predictors() predict(), with every predictor in newdata
pred_target_shp() predict(boundaries, aggregate)
plot() of pred_target_grid() and pred_target_shp() results plot_prediction(), or plot() of a predict() result
assess_pp() assess_prediction(), which takes models, size, metrics and control_mcmc for object, n_size, which_metric and control_sim, and "PIT" for "AnPIT"
plot_score(), plot_AnPIT() plot_cross_validation(), or plot() of an assess_prediction() result
assess_sim() assess_simulation(), which takes simulation, target, aggregate, boundaries, label, objective and breaks for obj_sim, f_grid_target, f_area_target, shp, col_names, pred_objective and categories, and spatial_scale = "location" for "grid"
summary() of assess_pp() and assess_sim() results summary() of assess_prediction() and assess_simulation() results
glgpm_sim(), surf_sim() simulate_glgpm(), with specify_glgpm() for a model given by its parameters and what = "surface" for surfaces
plot_sim_surf() plot_simulation(), or plot() of a simulate_glgpm() result
s_variogram(), plot_s_variogram() variogram() and plot_variogram(), with breaks for bins, n_permutations for n_permutation, and distance_crs and distance_units for convert_to_utm and scale_to_km
dist_summaries() summarise_distance(), with distance_crs and distance_units
propose_utm() propose_crs(), which chooses the CRS by its distortion of distances
convex_hull_sf() create_convex_hull()

check_mcmc() plot_mcmc(), with locations for component, and summarise_mcmc()
matern_cor() matern_correlation()
dast(), plot_mda() Removed. Models of mass drug administration move to a separate package
Laplace_sampling_MCMC(), maxim.integrand(), matern.grad.phi(), matern.hessian.phi(), compute_ID_coords() Removed. Their work is internal

Main changes

Fitting

  • glgpm() fits Gaussian, binomial, Poisson and negative binomial models with a spatial Gaussian process, gp(), and random effects, re(), and takes any link. Binomial, Poisson and negative binomial models are fitted by certified Monte Carlo maximum likelihood, which enlarges its samples until the Monte Carlo error of the estimates is small and reports a bound on that error. In binomial and Poisson fits, household effects whose children differ in covariates are integrated out, which makes such fits much faster.
  • Every parameter has one name, the same in start_pars, fixed_pars, coef(), profile() and parametric_bootstrap(), with tau2 for the variance of the nugget. glgpm_parameters() lists the parameters of a model and ?riskmap_parameters describes them. start_pars starts any of them, so start_pars = coef(fit) starts from another fit, and fixed_pars holds any of them, or all, in which case predict() works with the given values.
  • Data are sf objects. distance_crs and distance_units set the projection and the units of distances in every function that measures them, and propose_crs() proposes a projection that keeps distances accurate.
  • ?glgpm lists the components of a fit that code may rely on. logLik(), vcov() and nobs() work on fits, and with them AIC(), BIC() and update(). Every result records the version of RiskMap that made it.
  • set_control_mcmc() sets the number of draws it keeps in n_draws, and set_control_mcml() takes its sample sizes as initial_draws, validation_draws and max_draws.

Checking a fit

  • check_fit() reports how a fit was computed and flags anything that needs attention, profile() gives profile likelihoods and parametric_bootstrap() bootstrap intervals for the parameters.

Prediction

  • A single predict() method predicts at new locations or over the areas given in boundaries, with exceedance probabilities, population weights, standardisation and, if asked, the uncertainty of the estimated parameters. plot_prediction() maps the predictions, to_table() tabulates them, and assess_extrapolation() shows where they go beyond the data.
  • Predictions of Gaussian models with re() terms no longer depend on the labels of the groups, and joint predictions that include the random effects have the right covariance between them and the spatial process.
  • The covariates of the prediction grid tz_covariates now match those of tz_malaria. EVI, temperature, night-time light and precipitation come from the same rasters, so temperature is missing at 2 points and precipitation at 1, and ITN is a percentage with NA for missing values, where it was a proportion with -9999. The help pages give the source and units of each covariate, and population density is not in thousands, as they said.

Assessment and simulation

  • assess_prediction() compares models by spatial cross-validation. Every score is a loss, so lower is better, and PIT_area is given once for all test observations, next to its value under perfect calibration. Counts are scored with their exact distribution given the draws of the mean, where assess_pp() simulated them. specify_glgpm() and simulate_glgpm() simulate data and surfaces from a model, and assess_simulation() assesses predictions on them.
  • In assess_simulation() every value belongs to a class, those beyond the breaks to the end classes, covariates can have any name, and a prediction at a sampled location uses what the data say about its nugget.

Plots, printing and messages

  • Every plot has a function of its own, such as plot_variogram(), plot_prediction() and plot_cross_validation(), which plot() of the result also calls, so users can call either. Each returns one ggplot or patchwork object, which is drawn when printed. Methods and plot functions stop on an argument they don’t use.
  • Errors, warnings and messages are written with cli and have classes (?riskmap_conditions), long computations show their progress (?riskmap_progress), and options(RiskMap.messages = FALSE) silences the messages.
  • Packages that only some functions need, such as spatialsample and spatialEco for some splits of assess_prediction(), ggspatial for north arrows and scale bars, and jsonlite for get_worldpop(), are suggested rather than imported, and those functions ask for them.
  • RiskMap needs R 4.5.0 or later.
  • Custom links, the negative binomial family, the penalised complexity priors of set_control_mcml(), crs_distortion() and the spatial indicator of assess_extrapolation() are experimental and may change in a minor release, as their help pages say.
